concerns.message: The plan's delivery rule leaves no room for a free trigger that has nothing left to deliver. The property checker says "every free trigger is delivered in that step's message or the next boundary's", with no exception. But the emit only lists "still-eligible types from the older snapshot", and a type can drop out: the player gets the type back, or the older snapshot has no usable carrier entry. A common case is a fresh theft: in the older snapshot the victim still held the stolen copy, and the victim's own entries are excluded, while the other copies may have been sealed 30–60 s ago. intel-core-fixes had the exception "or dropped only because its type became ineligible, which the checker verifies". This plan doesn't repeat it.
concerns.consequence: A checker written as stated fails on ordinary property seeds. The worker then weakens it on the fly or drops the trigger silently. Either way a victim of a theft can get no lead at all, against §11's "give them a free fresh rumor", and the reviewers could block a third time.

concerns.message: The accumulator "starts with the player's pending set if a boundary was crossed", and when capped it "keeps the free types as the single pending set". Read literally, a capped step with no boundary builds an accumulator without the existing pending types and then replaces pending with only this step's free types. The same condition misfires at minute 28 when minute 28 isn't on a carrier boundary. That happens with compressed property-test configs; the real constants line up, since 1680 s is 56 × 30 s. There the cap lifts, a new trigger emits a message, and the older pending types still wait for the next boundary.
concerns.consequence: Earlier deferred types are overwritten and lost, or a pending type arrives in a second message. That breaks "learns about both at once", the rule this run exists to enforce, and the reviewers may find the same symptom again.

concerns.message: The plan doesn't say when a targeted request's eligibility is judged against the older snapshot. If it is judged when the request joins the accumulator, and on a boundary tick that happens before the snapshots rotate, the request can be answered `sighting` while the emitted message holds no entry for its type. The only outcomes the decision can give are `sighting` or `capped`, so it has no `none` for a type that has become ineligible.
concerns.consequence: The caller charges 25 gold for a sighting that was never delivered, which breaks intel-core's rule that gold is charged only when something is delivered (§11).

concerns.message: The rule that type order and sector choice must not depend on trigger order means generator draws must move to the single emit point, in sorted type order. Moving them changes how the seeded generator is used compared with the snapshot. Scripted tests that assert specific seeded sectors or rumor targets may change even when their scenario has nothing to do with batching.
concerns.consequence: Existing tests fail for reasons that have nothing to do with the findings. The worker must either change expectations, which the task allows only when reported, or keep draws per type and risk depending on trigger order. This uses up the new sixty-minute budget.

concerns.message: Finding 2's case, where every copy of a missing type is carried at the start, can't happen in real matches. At control start all 12 copies are sealed, and §2 bars late arrivals. So the new fallback, which moves the starting rumor to another missing type, is exercised only by the scripted test.
concerns.consequence: This is low risk. But if the start trigger can fire for a player who first appears after control start, for example on reconnect, the fallback changes generator use and replay hashes for those runs. Say which trigger counts as "start" in `docs/intel.md`.

simpler_alternative: Drop the \"if a boundary was crossed\" condition and use one rule for every player in every step. The accumulator is the pending set plus this step's triggers: losses, replacements and targeted sighting requests, each judged after the snapshots rotate. Emitting is allowed when the tick is at or past minute 28, or when no sighting has been sent for the current snapshot. If allowed, check eligibility once against the older snapshot, in sorted type order. Emit one message if any type is eligible and clear pending. Answer each targeted request `sighting` if its type is in the message and `none` otherwise. A type with nothing to deliver, or no message at all, uses up no cap. If not allowed, pending becomes the free part of the accumulator, which is a union because pending is in it, and targeted requests are answered `capped`. There is then one code path with no special case for boundaries or minute 28. The checker's exception becomes \"delivered, or ineligible at the emit that should have carried it\", and the checker can recompute that directly.
cheap_experiment: After restoring the snapshot, and before changing `step.ts`, add only the instrumentation to the existing seeded property runs. For each free trigger, record whether its type has any usable entry (one not held by the victim) in the older snapshot at the emit that should carry it. Also count steps with more than one sighting message per player. If free triggers with no usable entry are common, especially right after a theft, decide first whether they are dropped (and the checker exempts them) or kept pending until an entry appears. Also decide whether a targeted request in that state is answered `none`. Record those choices in `docs/intel.md` before rewriting the accumulator. The counts take minutes to get and settle the one rule the plan leaves open.
